headline: Europe's heat-and-drought season hardened into official numbers: the European Commission cut EU maize to 51.9 Mt from 59.9 Mt a month earlier and JRC MARS logged premature ripening, storm lodging and severe Hungarian drought, while Ghana's COCOBOD put next season's cocoa crop down at least 16%.
key_points: The European Commission's 30 July balance sheet cut EU 2026/27 maize production to 51.9 Mt from 59.9 Mt in June — an 8 Mt revision that lifts the EU's maize import requirement by 5.0 Mt to 24.0 Mt — with barley also cut to 51.1 Mt.

JRC MARS's July bulletin adds the ground-level detail behind the EU cuts: premature maturity and early harvesting across south-western Germany, Austria, Slovakia and Czechia; severe drought worst in Hungary; heat stress at maize flowering in northern Italy; and storm, downburst and hail lodging in northern Italy, Slovenia, Croatia and Germany.

AHDB's first 2026 UK harvest report extends the poor-cereals picture to the minor crops: spring barley at 5.3 t/ha and oats at 4.9 t/ha, both below their ten-year averages, alongside the already-recorded 6.8 t/ha wheat.

Ghana's COCOBOD told Reuters output will fall at least 16% in 2026/27, citing likely El Nino conditions and excessive May-June rain alongside disease and illegal mining; Ivory Coast is still expected down more than 10%, corroborating the existing July row.

POSITIVE counterweight this week: Montana spring wheat jumped 12 points in good-to-excellent, US winter wheat harvest hit 86% complete, Canadian Prairie canola conditions stayed favourable, and Turkiye's cool wet spring produced record winter crop yields — enough to push Paris rapeseed futures down 6.7% to £438.99/t.

conflicts.note: Both published 2026-08-03 and both attribute the move to weather, in opposite directions: Czapp reports Brazilian coffee futures UP at 331 while Barchart reports September ICE arabica (KCU26) DOWN 3.04% because dryness in Minas Gerais should accelerate the harvest. Different contracts and units; not reconciled, both rows kept.

Pre-existing and still open: AHDB's own outputs give 64% and 58% good-to-excellent for GB winter wheat on the same day, 2026-06-29. The series stays chartable:false on both the flag and the missing label.

France maize 2026 production: RFI (2026-08-08) says 9 Mt, COCERAL via World Grain (2026-07-10) says 9.4 Mt. Close but not identical; the gap is a month of further deterioration rather than a contradiction, recorded here so it is not read as one figure.
